answer: The Fused Graph Circuit ties wallet credibility to operator behavior. If a new node claims a willow identity, it inherits a liability flag from its first transaction. This exposure stretches until the network verifies the operator's real-world asset linkage. The horizon of this penalty shrinks only after a sustained period of honest activity logs. Without distinct legal entities, the attacker pays every fee and lost revenue from the spawned identities. This cost hits the zenith of their bandwidth budget when they sacrifice profitable jobs to keep the graph alive.
